newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's NRW state passes supplementary budget.
newsitem.headline: Germany's NRW state passes supplementary budget.

text.p: Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia (NRW), on Friday passed a supplementary 1997 budget to avert higher borrowing after tax revenue forecasts were revised down.

The 'red-green' coalition government of Social Democrats (SPD) and environmentalist Greens passed NRW Finance Minister Heinz Schleusser's package of 1.8 billion marks ($1 billion) in savings to make up for the expected shortfall in revenues this year.
The package included 500 million marks in departmental spending cuts, while sales of state property -- including a 50 percent stake in Duesseldorf airport -- should raise a further 500 million marks.
Remaining cuts of 800 million marks will come from savings in personnel and debt service costs.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel's federal budget deficit makes up only around half of total public sector new borrowing at federal, state and local government level this year.
Waigel has pledged to keep the public sector deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, enabling Germany to qualify for the planned 1999 start of Europe's single currency.
